title: QAI Resolution
description: Machine cache for one journey, specific to a platform and regenerable. Written by QAI, versioned in git so that CI replays without a model call and so that a self-repair shows up as a reviewable diff. Do not edit by hand.

version.description: Version of the resolution format, not of the application. Absent means 1. It goes up when the observation changes (v2) or when the meaning of a stored field changes (v3: a relative urlEquals value is resolved against the base URL; actions may be empty for a verification-only step). A file is written with the lowest version its content needs. A QAI refuses a file newer than the version it reads.

scenario.description: Id of the scenario this file resolves.

recordedAt.description: When the resolution was generated. Used to date a resolution that has become suspect.

appVersion.description: Version of the application under test at recording time, when it is known.

steps.description: One entry per step, keyed on the scenario step id. That anchor is what lets an intent be reworded without invalidating its cache.

role.description: The subset of roles that exists on all three platforms. Mappings in docs/driver.md.

locator.description: Semantic targeting: what the user sees, never a selector.

name.description: Accessible name, exact or partial. May reference a capture via {{name}}.

nth.description: Index among the matches. Without it, several matches means the engine refuses to act.

fallback.description: Platform-specific technical fallback, tried only if primary fails. A fallback that gets used is a signal: the application's accessibility has degraded.

action.description: One primitive gesture. An intent often translates into several.

value.description: Template, interpolated at the moment of acting: {{capture}}, or {{env.NAME}} for a value read from the environment. A secret must never be written here in clear text — this file lives in git.

oneOf.description: Drops files into an input[type=file], even a hidden one.

files.description: Paths relative to the scenario file. An absolute path would only replay on the machine that wrote it, and any path leaving the scenario directory is refused.

oneOf.description: Arms the answer to the next native dialog. Goes RIGHT BEFORE the gesture that triggers it: the dialog blocks the page from the click onwards, so there is no moment after it to answer.

check.description: Machine form of an assertion. The key it is stored under is the exact text of the scenario's assertion.

oneOf.description: Check on the current address. No target: a URL is not a node. urlEquals: a relative value (".", "orders?id=3", "/login") is resolved against the run's base URL, then compared strictly; an absolute value is compared raw; an empty or blank value is never resolved and fails. urlContains: raw substring. Trailing slash, query and fragment are always part of what is asserted.
Step watchdog: bears on what the application DID, not on what it displays. Evaluated once, outside the re-evaluation window.

allow.description: Tolerated URL or message fragments, so that a noisy third-party integration does not teach the team to switch the watchdog off.

actions.description: The gestures that carry out the intent, in order. Assertions and captures are evaluated once, after the last one. Empty if and only if the step is verification-only (no intent on this platform).

captures.description: Values extracted from the screen, reusable further on via {{name}}.

assertions.description: Key = the exact text of the scenario's assertion. The healer is never allowed to touch these.

healedAt.description: Timestamp of the last repair, null if the resolution is original.

healNote.description: What the healer understood of the change, for the human reviewing the diff.
